title: Machine Learning Techniques for the Identification of Risk Factors Associated with Food Insecurity among Adults in Arab countries during the COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: In the Corona Cooking Survey analysis of 13,443 adults across Arab countries, 9.3% were classified as food insecure; prevalence was highest in Jordan, Palestine, Lebanon, and Saudi Arabia. On a balanced subset of 4,259, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest achieved reported accuracy of 81.6% and 81.4%; SHAP ranked country and age among key predictors. These are cross-sectional associations, not causal risk factors. The primary v1 describes a 70:20:10 train/test/validation split and 10-fold tuning. This is internal evaluation on the study survey, not external validation; the authors report limited country-specific sample sizes.
ai_technology: Seven machine-learning algorithms classified Food Consumption Score groups; SHAP feature analysis ranked country, age, financial difficulty, depression, and food access among the most influential predictors.
